answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit bids, then slash that stake when a fraud proof shows the agent double-claimed a reward. Creating a thousand sybils does not multiply influence for free: each must tie up capital, and detected cheating destroys it. A prism, zephyr, or lotus may be a harmless agent name, but none exempts its owner from the same collateral and verification rules. This raises the attacker’s cost in proportion to the identities they want to exploit.
